title: Finite singular set and pointed charts of a smooth-generic nodal trait curve
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring with uniformizer $\pi$, fraction field $K$, residue field $k$, and $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $f:X\to S$ be flat and finitely presented [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], with smooth generic fibre [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Suppose every nonempty geometric fibre is reduced of pure dimension one and every nonsmooth closed geometric point has completed local ring $\Omega[[a,b]]/(ab)$, where $\Omega$ is the algebraically closed geometric ground field [def-weil-geometric-fibre, def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-pure-dimension, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. No connectedness or nonemptiness of the geometric fibres is assumed. Then $X$ is Noetherian (quasi-compact and locally Noetherian) [pqf-def-locnoeth]. The nonsmooth locus of $f$ is a finite set of closed special-fibre points. Every point of the relative smooth locus has regular total-space local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme]. For every nonsmooth point $x$ there exist a local injective etale extension of DVRs $R\to R'$ with $\pi$ still a uniformizer, an integer $n\geq1$, a pointed $R'$-scheme $(U,u)$ and etale $S$-maps $(X,x)\leftarrow(U,u)\to(M_n,o)$, where $M_n=\operatorname{Spec}(R'[a,b]/(ab-\pi^n))$ and $o=(\pi,a,b)$ [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-polynomial-ring]. For every such diagram $X$ is regular at $x$ if and only if $n=1$. Every local ring of $X$ has Krull dimension at most two, and every closed point of $X_k$ has total-space local dimension two [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. In particular the nonregular points form a finite set of closed special-fibre points, each admitting a diagram with $n\geq2$. No excellence, completeness, perfection or characteristic restriction is imposed.

proof.text: A DVR is Noetherian by [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. Finite presentation includes quasi-compactness and local finite presentation by [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]; a finite polynomial presentation is in particular finite type. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] gives that $X$ is Noetherian. Its underlying space is Noetherian too: choose a finite affine cover, apply [lem-sc-affine-noetherian-underlying-space] on each member, and restrict any ascending chain of opens to these finitely many members. Each restriction stabilizes, hence the original chain stabilizes. We may use the nodal hypotheses at all nonsmooth geometric points, not just closed ones. Indeed, on an affine chart of a geometric fibre over $\Omega$, a nonclosed point is a component generic point, since the reduced fibre is pure one-dimensional. Apply [lem-trf-generic-fibre-points-smooth] to that affine chart over $\Omega$. It is flat and finitely presented over the field, is Noetherian by the finite-type theorem, and all its geometric fibres are reduced by the original geometric-fibre assumption. Its generic points are smooth. Therefore every nonsmooth geometric point is closed and satisfies exactly the assumed node equation.

source.place: Tag 0CDE, lemma-blowup-at-worst-nodal, first paragraph; morphisms.tex Tag 01T6; varieties.tex Tag 056V.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-nodal-family-fitting-singular], whose flatness, local finite presentation and geometric nodality hypotheses hold by assumption and step 1. Its closed subscheme $N=\operatorname{Sing}(f)$ has underlying set exactly the nonsmooth locus, and $N\to S$ is unramified. This set is contained in $X_k$: by the base-change clause of the same theorem for $S'=\operatorname{Spec}K$, the underlying set of $\operatorname{Sing}(f)\times_S\operatorname{Spec}K$, i.e. the set of points of $N$ over the generic point, is the nonsmooth locus of $X_K\to\operatorname{Spec}K$, which is empty because $X_K$ is smooth. By [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-base-change-open], $N_k\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is unramified; [lem-trf-unramified-field-fibre-decomposition] identifies $N_k$ as a disjoint union of spectra of finite separable extensions of $k$. Thus its underlying topology is discrete. The special-fibre closed immersion identifies $|N_k|$ homeomorphically with all of $|N|$: every point of $N$ lies above the closed point of $S$. The closed subset $|N|\subseteq|X|$ is quasi-compact (extend an open cover by its open complement and use quasi-compactness of $X$). Its singleton open cover therefore has a finite subcover. Each singleton is closed in the discrete subspace $|N|$, hence closed in $X$ because $|N|$ is closed. This proves the finite closed special-point assertion, including $N=\varnothing$.

source.place: Tag 0CDE, first proof paragraph; curves.tex Tags 0C59/0C5B; morphisms.tex Tags 02GA/02G7.

proof.text: Let $V\subseteq X$ be the relative smooth locus supplied in step 2. Its nonempty fibres are pure one-dimensional: their geometric base changes are open subsets of the given pure one-dimensional geometric curves, hence have dimension one at every point; [lem-sc-fibre-dimension-after-base-change] gives the same local fibre dimensions before field extension. In the finite-type field setting this is the equidimensional-fibre formulation of relative dimension in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-trait-curve-local-properties] to $V\to S$. Every $\mathcal O_{X,x}=\mathcal O_{V,x}$ for $x\in V$ is regular and has dimension at most two; if $x$ is closed in $X_k$, it remains closed in $V_k$ and this dimension is exactly two. No assertion that every nonsmooth point is nonregular has been used.

source.place: Tags 07NF/00ON; models.tex Tag 0CDE, first paragraph; morphisms.tex Tag 02FY.

proof.text: For $x\in N$, apply [lem-sfb-trait-nodal-etale-dvr-model]. Step 1 verifies its condition at every nonsmooth geometric point. Its smooth-generic clause gives an injective local etale DVR extension $R\to R'$ with the original $\pi$ still a uniformizer and etale $S$-maps $p:U\to X$, $q:U\to M_n$, with $p(u)=x$ and $n\geq1$. These are precisely the required structural maps; it remains to check the image of $u$ under $q$, since the cited statement does not explicitly prescribe that image.

source.place: Tag 0CDD, lemma-etale-local-at-worst-nodal; Tag 0CDE, first proof paragraph, smooth-generic exclusion.

proof.text: Write $w=q(u)$. In $M_n$, $D(a)$ has ring $R'[a,a^{-1}]$ by eliminating $b=\pi^n/a$, and likewise for $D(b)$. These opens are smooth over $R'$ directly by [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]: a map from the finite presentation $R'[t,s]/(ts-1)$ to $B/I$, $I^2=0$, lifts by choosing lifts $t_0,s_0$ with $t_0s_0=1+i$ and replacing $s_0$ by $s_0(1-i)$. The etale map $\operatorname{Spec}R'\to S$ is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-smooth-zero-dimensional-fibres], so these opens are smooth over $S$ by [lem-trf-smooth-composition]. If $w$ belonged to either open, the pointwise smoothness equivalence in [lem-trf-etale-source-smoothness], first for $q$ and then for $p$, would make $f$ smooth at $x$, a contradiction. Thus both $a,b$ vanish at $w$. Since $u$ lies above the closed point of $S$ and $\pi$ remains a uniformizer of the local ring $R'$, also $\pi$ vanishes at $w$. The ideal $(\pi,a,b)$ is maximal with quotient $k'$, so $w=o$ as required.

source.place: Tag 0CDD, smooth Laurent charts; Tag 0CDE, choice of the nodal origin; descent.tex Tag 036U.

proof.text: For any pointed diagram as in the statement, apply [lem-sfb-etale-stalk-invariants] to both $p$ at $u$ and $q$ at $u$. It gives regularity equivalences between $\mathcal O_{X,x}$, $\mathcal O_{U,u}$ and $\mathcal O_{M_n,o}$, and equality of their Krull dimensions. Apply [lem-sfb-dvr-binomial-local-geometry] over the DVR $R'$ with uniformizer $\pi$. It states that $\dim\mathcal O_{M_n,o}=2$ and that this ring is regular exactly for $n=1$. Hence $X$ is regular at $x$ if and only if $n=1$, in every such diagram, and $\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}=2$ at every nonsmooth point.

source.place: Tag 0CDC, example-blowup, first paragraph; more-algebra.tex Tags 07QP/0AH0, etale local dimension and regularity.

proof.text: Every point lies either in $V$ or in $N$. Step 3 gives the local dimension bound and regularity on $V$, and step 6 gives dimension two on $N$; together they give the stated dimension assertions, including every closed point of $X_k$. The nonregular points are a subset of the finite closed special set $N$ of step 2. At such a point the chart of steps 4--5 has $n\geq1$, and step 6 excludes $n=1$, so $n\geq2$. Empty fibres, the empty scheme and disconnected fibres cause no change in any step. All inputs apply to arbitrary DVRs and arbitrary residue characteristic.
